title: MYTH BUSTER CONTINUATION — JANUS / Vault 87 Protective Refusal Hypothesis
scope: Test the hypothesis that keeping the Little Lamplight access door to Vault 87 closed protected the children from a lethal experimental institution, while strictly separating the protective outcome from the unresolved identity, knowledge, and intention of the responder inside the Vault.

core_observation.outside_group: The founding Little Lamplighters, led by Jason Grant, repeatedly seek admission through the Vault 87-side access door.
core_observation.inside_environment: Vault 87 contains the Evolutionary Experimentation Program, modified FEV human experimentation, concealed deaths, and institutional secrecy.
core_observation.historical_outcome: The children remain outside Vault 87 and instead survive by creating Little Lamplight as a self-governing settlement.

protective_refusal_hypothesis.compressed: THE CLOSED DOOR MAY HAVE SAVED THE CHILDREN.
logic: Vault 87 was demonstrably dangerous to its own residents.
EEP-linked deaths were concealed under undefined/unexplained coding.
The children requested entry but were not admitted.
By remaining outside, they avoided incorporation into the Vault 87 institutional environment.
They survived long enough to establish Little Lamplight and a durable social order.
protective_refusal_hypothesis.result: The closed door had a protective consequence regardless of whether that consequence was intended by the responder.

intent_boundary.rule: A protective consequence must not be promoted into proof of protective intent without an independent identity and motive binding.

peter_stevens_conditional_model.premise: If Peter Stevens was the man who answered the children, his known circumstances create a coherent protective-refusal interpretation.
known_context: Peter Stevens had lost his son Jason Stevens inside Vault 87.
Jason Stevens appears in final-game medical records under UD000, the code associated with concealed special-EEP-section deaths.
Peter repeatedly hears children's laughter in the outer tunnels.
Vault doctors interpret those sounds as grief-related hallucination rather than independently checking the external source.
Peter's surviving writings show despair about raising children inside Vault 87 and profound distrust of life inside the Vault.
peter_stevens_conditional_model.conditional_interpretation: A father who had lost his own child inside a lethal institution could plausibly refuse entry to living children because he believed entering the Vault meant death, even if he did not know the exact EEP mechanism.
peter_stevens_conditional_model.forbidden_upgrade: Do not state that Peter deliberately saved Jason Grant unless the answering-man identity is independently established.

outside.name: Jason Grant
outside.role: founding Little Lamplighter and future first mayor

middle.name: Peter Stevens
middle.role: inside-side witness who hears children in outer tunnels

meaning_to_children: evidence that adults will not save them

possible_meaning_if_responder_understood: denial of entry into an unsafe environment
keeping children outside the experimental system

two_faces_of_the_closed_door.janus_interpretation: One physical threshold supports two opposed meanings depending on the observer's side: abandonment from outside and possible protection from inside.

canonical_inversion.registry_parent_rule: The adult must arrive before chronic danger forces the child to become their own armor.
vault87_case: The children interpret the refusal as abandonment.
Yet entry into Vault 87 may have exposed them to a lethal experimental institution.
Therefore the adult protective act, if intentional, would consist not in opening the door but in refusing passage through a dangerous threshold.
canonical_inversion.compressed: THE ADULT MAY SAVE THE CHILD NOT BY OPENING THE DOOR, BUT BY KEEPING THE WRONG DOOR CLOSED.

janus_guardian_rule_extension.extension: A guardian of a threshold is not defined by opening every door. Guardianship includes preserving the distinction between safe passage and destructive passage.
janus_guardian_rule_extension.boundary: This is a JANUS interpretive rule derived from comparison with the Fallout 3 case; it is not attributed to Bethesda.

signal_interpretation_layer.external_signal: Real children are present outside Vault 87.
signal_interpretation_layer.inside_witness: Peter Stevens hears children's laughter in the outer tunnels.
signal_interpretation_layer.institutional_model: Vault doctors interpret the signal through Peter's grief over his dead son Jason.
signal_interpretation_layer.forensic_result: The presence of an independently documented outside group makes a purely hallucinatory explanation insufficient for the shared event class.
signal_interpretation_layer.lesson: Correct perception can coexist with an incorrect explanatory model; an institution can dismiss a real signal by fitting it to a plausible but incomplete prior.

cross_registry_links.relation: Adult protection before the child becomes their own armor.
cross_registry_links.vault87_extension: Protective adulthood may require refusing a dangerous passage rather than granting access.

cross_registry_links.relation: Janus as guardian of threshold and witness of both sides.
cross_registry_links.vault87_extension: The same closed door has opposed meanings on opposite sides; neither side should be erased.

cross_registry_links.relation: Separate signal, interpretation, and response; distress is data before judgment.
cross_registry_links.vault87_extension: A real child-signal is heard but institutionally interpreted as grief-related hallucination.

cross_registry_links.relation: External witnesses should be admitted epistemically even when physical or operational authority remains bounded.
cross_registry_links.vault87_extension: Vault 87 exhibits the opposite governance pattern: the external signal is not independently checked and the physical door stays closed.

cross_registry_links.relation: Independent witness structure and negative controls.
cross_registry_links.vault87_extension: Jason Grant and Peter Stevens preserve opposite-side evidence for the same cross-boundary signal class.

anti_overfit_rules: Do not convert survival after refusal into proof of benevolent intent.
Do not identify Peter Stevens as the answering man without a direct game binding.
Do not claim the responder knew FEV or EEP details unless explicit evidence is found.
Do not treat the name Jason appearing on both sides as proof of deliberate Janus encoding.
Do not convert Janus symbolism into Bethesda authorial intent.
Preserve the possibility that the same action can be experienced as rejection and function retrospectively as protection.

ru: Иногда закрытая дверь — не отказ от спасения, а само спасение.
Ребёнок снаружи видел отказ; взрослый внутри мог видеть смертельный порог.
Мы подтверждаем защитный исход, но не приписываем человеку намерение без доказательства.
Хранитель порога обязан знать не только когда открыть дверь, но и когда не позволить пройти через неё.
Два свидетеля по разные стороны двери важнее одной удобной интерпретации.
en: Sometimes a closed door is not the refusal of rescue but the rescue itself.
The child outside saw rejection; the adult inside may have seen a lethal threshold.
We confirm the protective outcome without inventing protective intent.
A guardian of the threshold must know not only when to open a door, but when passage itself must be refused.
Two witnesses on opposite sides of a door outweigh one convenient interpretation.
